name: otr-many-facts
about: An over-the-road job with many facts: enough for five angles that differ in kind.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: Family owned, and the owner still drives

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook equipment_first (equipment first) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $402.10 in the last 28 days over 30100 impressions and brought 14 leads, $28.72 per lead.

output.audience: Experienced Class A over-the-road drivers running long lanes, reefer or similar. They may now drive older trucks or handle freight by hand. A plain pay per mile, a newer truck, freight they do not unload and a pet in the cab would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a reefer truck rolling on an open highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile and the states its lanes cover.
angles.why: Pay is the clearest fact on the sheet, and long lanes make a per-mile rate matter. This hook has not been measured here yet.

angles.idea: Lead with the newer truck, parked and clean with the reefer trailer hooked up.
angles.proof: The job lists newer trucks and reefer freight.
angles.why: Our earlier ads with this hook and scene brought leads at a cost per lead under the benchmark pause line. The lead count is modest, so treat it as a good sign, not proof.

angles.idea: From the driver's seat, state plainly what the job asks: Class A, over-the-road reefer, and the years and weeks figures.
angles.proof: The job states the licence class, a years figure, a weeks figure and the states covered.
angles.why: No lead outcomes have been measured, so stating requirements up front guards against unfit leads. The office should confirm what the years and weeks figures mean before writing.

angles.idea: Lead with what the driver comes back to: a quiet home street, with the benefits that cover life off the truck.
angles.proof: The job lists health insurance, a retirement plan and paid time off.
angles.why: Benefits matter most to drivers thinking past the next load, and this scene carries them without promising a schedule. Nothing has been measured for this hook.

angles.idea: On a plain plate, lead with the owner who still drives, then name the daily details of the work as facts.
angles.proof: The carrier is family owned and the owner still drives; the job's details cover a pet in the cab and freight the driver does not unload.
angles.why: An owner who drives is a claim drivers can check, and it sets this carrier apart from larger fleets. Untested here, so judge it on early results.
